body:
Preview audio works. The editor routed every clip through Web Audio, and Chromium mutes a MediaElementAudioSourceNode when the media comes from another origin - which is exactly what the asset protocol is. Previews now play straight from the media element, and export builds its own mixer from same-origin blob URLs so recordings keep their sound.

Editing got quicker and smoother:

- Clips and clip edges follow the pointer exactly and only snap when you let go
- Edge handles are wider and always visible, with a grip
- `[` / `]` or `Q` / `W` trim to the playhead, and the inspector has start/end trim buttons plus -1s/+1s
- `Alt+arrow` nudges the selected clip one frame (`Shift` for ten)
- Double-click a title clip, or the text itself in the monitor, to edit its words
- Image clips are no longer limited to their 5 second source length

### Downloading

The installer is 157 MB, and this network kept dropping large TLS uploads, so it is attached as eight 20 MB parts. Clone the repo and run:

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\download-installer.ps1
```

That downloads every part, joins them into `Tacot-Edit-Setup-0.2.3.exe` in your temp folder, checks the size, and launches it.
